title: DCP Adaptive Hybrid Classical-Quantum Peeling Sample-Complexity Bridge
claims: Native independent X parity has mean gamma^h*product(cos(theta_i)), not gamma^h*cos(sum(theta_i)). Modular phase-bearing classical samples are not supplied by the input.
An explicit uniform-even-Y signed product-Pauli protocol has mean 2^(1-h)*gamma^h*cos(sum(theta_i)); this is one legal separable competitor, not an optimality bound.
The public star-CNOT circuit retains all measured syndromes and yields conditional visibility gamma^h at the realized signed label. No hidden secret chooses its gates.

For the coarsened matched-cosine coin at zero cosine, retained erasures give local Fisher information p*gamma^(2h), whereas fair-coin replacement gives p^2*gamma^(2h). Neither is a discrete-secret recovery bound.
No classical dominance, all-receiver no-go, DCP decoder or asymptotic quantum advantage is established.
